title: ConfigMap Update Not Taking Effect
intro: A teammate updated a ConfigMap value an hour ago but the app is still using the old value. They're confused because 'the ConfigMap shows the new value.'

steps.prompt: Confirm the ConfigMap does show the updated value.
steps.hint: Just confirm what the teammate said.

steps.prompt: Check the running pod app-6b7c8d9-mnopq to see what environment it's actually using.
steps.hint: Get a shell or run env inside a live pod to see what it actually loaded.

steps.prompt: Confirmed — the pod is still running with the old value baked into its environment. Check how long the pod has been running.
steps.fake_output:
NAME                    READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
app-6b7c8d9-mnopq       1/1     Running   0          6h
steps.hint: Compare the pod's age to when the ConfigMap was changed.

steps.prompt: The pod is older than the ConfigMap change. Trigger a rollout restart so pods pick up the new values.
steps.hint: ConfigMaps mounted as env vars are only read at container start — updating the ConfigMap alone doesn't push the change to already-running pods.

steps.prompt: Confirm the new pods have the updated value.
steps.hint: Wait for the rollout, then you could exec in again to double check env if you wanted.

resolution: This is one of the most common ConfigMap gotchas: updating a ConfigMap does NOT automatically restart pods that consumed it as environment variables — those were baked in at container start. (Note: if the ConfigMap were mounted as a volume/file instead of env vars, the file contents would update live, though the app would still need to notice and reload it.) The fix is a rollout restart to force new pods to start fresh and pick up the current values.
